*** * *
 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 9.7.2023 at about 6.15 p.m. the petitioner was walking on the left side of the road, near Pathanjali store, infront of Amman Hotel, Bhuvaneshwari Layout,
Naganathapura, Bengaluru, at that time driver of Omni car bearing registration No.KA- 51-MJ-9857 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Blossom Hospital,
wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and undergone 3 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 surgery and she had spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards her medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment.
4.
It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner hale & healthy, aged about 53 years, doing tailoring and house wife and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, she could not able to do any work as earlier.
5. It is stated that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of Omni car bearing registration No.KA-51-MJ-9857.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver of offending vehicle by the jurisdictional Electronic City Police, in Crime No.237/2023.
As such, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Other hand, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court, remained absent, hence, he was placed exparte.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.1, it is contended that the petition is not 4 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

Further it has denied the manner in which the accident took place, injuries sustained, age, avocation and income of the petitioner and also expenses incurred towards medication and other incidental charges.

The respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Omni car bearing registration No.KA-51-MJ-9857 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It is the defense of the respondent No.1 that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.

It is also the contention of this respondent that the compensation and interest Menaka vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67383749/
2 claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant.

sentences.text: Upon these grounds, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 9.7.2023 at about 6.15 pm near Pathanjali stores, infront of Amman Hotel,
5 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 Bhuvaneshwari Layout, Naganathapura, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Omni car bearing registration No.KA-51-MJ-9857 in an actionable negligence?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, she herself examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.

In addition to this, placed the evidence of Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. as PW2 and got marked documents as Ex.P16 & Ex.P17.
10.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not placed any evidence on its behalf.

11. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.
12.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
6 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-

13. It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Omni car bearing registration No.KA-51-MJ- 9857, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently she had sustained grievous injuries.

14. On the other hand, the respondent No.1, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 remained absent, placed exparte.
15. The petitioner in order to prove her case, examined herself as PW1.
PW1 in her examination-in- chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon police documents, marked at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
Ex. P1-true copy of the F.I.R.
Ex . P2
-true copy of the first information statement.
Ex. P3-true copy of spot mahazar,

Ex.P4- Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P5- reply to the said notice, Ex.P6-true copy of IMV report,

16. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Electronic City Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of IPC.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
17.

Apart from this, though the respondent has disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, but not examined either the driver of the offending vehicle or any other independent eye witness who witnessed the accident.

18. At the time of cross-examination of PW1, nothing has been elicited from his mouth to disbelieve the assertion of the petitioner and to prove all the defenses forthcoming in the written statement of the respondent.

In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Omni car bearing registration No.KA-51-MJ-9857.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
20.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

21. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
9 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.

The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as Menaka vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67383749/
4 money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

entities.text: Menaka vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation."

Pain and Sufferings;
22. PW1 has stated in her evidence that, she has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries she has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, she had sustained the following injuries:-
10 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 1) Right shoulder GT fracture with dislocation 2) Left Knee Proximal tibia fracture 3) Acetabulum anterior wall fracture 4) Patella hair line fracture 5) Right eye brow cut laceration wound 23.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P11 issued by Blossom Hospital reveals that the petitoner was admitted on 9.7.2023 and discharged on 15.7.2023.
Further she has palced laboratory report and OP sheet at Ex.P14 & Ex.P15.
In addition to their evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. as PW2.

He has stated that the petitioner has sustained right shoulder GT fracture with dislocation, left knee proximal tibia fracture acetabulum anterior wall fracture, patella fracture and right eye brow cut lacerated wound.
He has placed clinical note and x-ray as per Ex.P16 & Ex.P17.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, she could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

11 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 Loss of income during treatment period:
24.
PW1 has stated that, she was working as a tailor and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

She has not placed any documents to show that she was earning Rs.25,000/-
per month.
In such a situation notational income is apt to be taken by applying the same principle like other cases.

On going through the discharge summary issued by the Blossom Hospital marked at Ex.P11 reveals that the petitioner was admitted on Menaka vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67383749/
5 9.7.2023 and discharged on 15.7.2023.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to her to do daily routine work at least for a period of two months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by her.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.32,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
25.
The petitioner in connection with her treatment expenses, she has placed medical bills as per Ex.P12 to the extent of Rs.2,74,703/- along with prescriptions at Ex.P13.
There are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bills.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,74,703/- under the head of medical expenses.

12 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
26.
The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient and also as an outpatient.

During that period, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment,
conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
Loss of future income;
27. The petitioner herein, asserting that, she had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by her.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on her evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.

As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P10 goes to show that, she had sustained grievous injuries, for which, she took the treatment as an inpatient and also as an outpatient.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed discharge summaries for consideration.
Apart from this, another material 13 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 witness by name Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. examined as PW2.

PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained right shoulder GT fracture with dislocation,
left knee proximal tibia fracture acetabulum anterior wall fracture, patella fracture and right eye brow cut lacerated wound.
For which the petitioner underwent surgery in the form of ORIF with plate and screws for proximal tibia and ORIF with CC screws for GT fracture.

He has placed clinical notes and x-ray as per Ex.P16 & Ex.P17.
28.
On examination of the petitioner, he has healed surgical scar mark over knee and shoulder, mild swelling of leg, ankle and deltoid wasting, altered pigmentation over the surgical scar mark.
X-ray shows shoulder fracture united with implant in situ.
PW2 assessed the disability from right upper limb and left lower limb to whole body is 20%

6 29.

sentences.text: At the time of cross-examination of PW2, he admitted that he is not the treated doctor.
Fracture is united.
This witness also denied the suggestion that, petitioner has not sustained any permanent disability and he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.

Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW2 by following the guidelines issued by Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Government of India and accordingly petitioner has 20% disability of whole body.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 15% instead of 20%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
31. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 53 years.
The petitioner in order to prove her age she has not placed any document.

On perusal of wound certificate marked at Ex.P10,
the age of the petitioner was mentioned as 53 years.
From this document, it can be said that the petitioner was aged about 53 years at the time of accident.

To the said age as per Sarla Verma case,
multiplier '11' is to be taken into consideration.
32. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in her evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident, she was doing tailoring work and was earning Rs.25,000/-.
But she has not placed any document to show her income.
In 15 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2023.

As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- for the year 2023.
33.

In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of her future, in a slight manner, to do her daily routine work, as well as to do her work for livelihood on going through her age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.16,000 X 12 X 11 X15/100= Rs.3,16,800/-.
Loss of amenities;
34.
As noted above, the petitioner has sustained fractures in the accident as a result she has permanent partial disability.
The petitioner was aged about 53 years at the time of the accident.

The said disability certainly affects not only on her avocation, but also affects on her amenities as the petitioner could not able to enjoy her life as she was enjoying earlier prior to the 16 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 accident.
By overall considering these aspects it is just and proper to award Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.

7 35.

sentences.text: In connection with the future medication, PW2 has stated that the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants, which costs about Rs.30,000/-.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head future medical expenses.

36. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 50,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 32,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs.2,74,703-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 10,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.3,16,800-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 20,000-00 7.
Future medication Rs. 20,000-00 Total Rs.7,23,503-00 17 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 37.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,23,503/- (Rupees seven lakh twenty three thousand five hundred and three only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

entities.text: Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

LIABILITY:
38.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Omni car bearing registration No.KA-51-MJ-9857, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
39. As per the records, the insurance policy in respect of Omni car bearing No.KA-51-MJ-9857 is valid from 17.12.2022 to 16.12.2023.
The alleged accident occurred on 9.7.2023.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being insurance company and the respondent No.2 being owner of the offending vehicle 18 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
40.

In view of my due discussions on point Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.7,23,503/- (Rupees seven lakh twenty three thousand five hundred and three only), along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance police the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from 19 SCCH-18 MVC No.4728/2023 the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
